name: core.openwop.workflows.devops
description: Real-work workflow pack — the DevOps cluster: senior-style code review of a diff, changelog/release-notes drafting from a commit log, CI-failure diagnosis from a signature-verified webhook, and a stale-issue gardener over the public GitHub API. All four are ADVISORY — they analyze and notify in-app, never write to your repo or post comments (an authenticated GitHub write path would bind a connection behind an approval gate; deferred until the MCP-reach connection binding has a chain precedent). These chains do not run the Code Reviewer / Git Author AGENTS — those remain chat-drivable via the agents surface; the chains use short chain-local prompts over core.ai.chatCompletion. All tenant values are run parameters (replay-deterministic).
author: openwop

chains.label: Diff Review (advisory)
chains.description: Paste a diff (or pipe one from a webhook) and get a senior-style review — correctness, security, and test-coverage findings, each citing file and line, ranked by severity. Advisory only: it notifies you in-app and never posts to your repo.

config.systemPrompt: You are a senior engineer reviewing a diff. Report findings in severity order (correctness first, then security, then tests/maintainability), each citing file:line from the diff and stating the concrete failure scenario. If the diff is clean, say so plainly. Do not invent context beyond the diff. Diff: {{params.diffText}}

review.description: The severity-ordered review with file:line citations.

chains.label: Release Notes Drafter
chains.description: Turn a commit log (git log --oneline or richer) into a changelog entry and human-readable release notes — grouped by added/changed/fixed, with breaking changes called out first. Drafted to a notification; paste it wherever your release lives.

commitLog.description: The commit log for the release range.

audience.description: Who the release notes are written for.

config.systemPrompt: From this commit log, draft: (1) a changelog entry grouped Added / Changed / Fixed / Security, breaking changes first and clearly marked; (2) short release notes readable by {{params.audience}} — what improved and why it matters, no commit hashes. Be faithful to the log; do not invent features. Log: {{params.commitLog}}

notes.description: The changelog entry plus release notes draft.

chains.label: CI Failure Explainer
chains.description: Bind your CI's webhook via the trigger-subscriptions API (signature-verified — the secret stays host-side) and every failed run arrives as a diagnosis, not a wall of logs: the failing step, the probable cause, and the first thing to try. CI-specialized analysis — for generic webhook routing use the starter Verified Webhook Router.

family.description: Webhook signature family: github, stripe, slack, or raw-hmac.

config.systemPrompt: You are a CI-failure analyst. From this CI webhook payload (workflow run / check suite / job logs excerpt), report: the failing step, the probable root cause in one sentence, the evidence, and the single first thing to try. If the payload is not a failure event, say so in one line.

diagnosis.description: The failing step, probable cause, and first fix to try.

chains.label: Stale-Issue Gardener
chains.description: Point it at a public GitHub repo and get a gardener's report over the least-recently-updated open issues: which look answered or obsolete (close candidates), which need a nudge, and a suggested comment for each. Advisory only — it never posts; works unauthenticated on public repos (private repos need a GitHub connection — coming later).

repo.description: The public GitHub repo as owner/name (e.g. openwop/openwop).

config.systemPrompt: You are an issue gardener for {{params.repo}}. From these least-recently-updated open issues (SKIP any entry with a pull_request field — those are PRs, not issues), produce: CLOSE CANDIDATES (looks answered/obsolete — say why), NEEDS A NUDGE (waiting on someone — who), and a one-line suggested comment for each. Be specific; cite issue numbers and titles.

report.description: Close candidates, nudge list, and suggested comments.
